rationale: The managers' question is why patients return, and the retrieved evidence shows the answer lies in decisions made at home by patients, carers and clinicians (c2, c3, c4). An interview study with purposive samples of each group, anchored to recent readmissions, answers that directly; a rate comparison would repeat the dashboard and struggle with case mix (c1). Reporting follows SRQR.
alternatives: Record review of readmissions only (refused: records rarely capture what patients and carers understood)
Matched cohort comparison with ward care (refused: explains how often, not why)
Mixed methods with a new survey (deferred: the interviews should come first)
whyNotMoreComplex: A mixed-methods design would add a survey instrument that does not exist yet; the interviews will show what, if anything, is worth counting.

decision.statement: Pursue a qualitative study of recent readmissions from the program, interviewing patients, carers and clinicians in separate groups, because carer and clinician night-time decisions (c2, c3) and carer breakdown (c4) are plausible routes that local counts cannot explain, and 12 to 20 interviews per group can give adequate information (c5).
decision.question: What study should the program run to explain its readmissions before adding beds?

criteria.text: Plausible routes to readmission exist that only participants can explain.
Case mix alone explains the dashboard gap, leaving nothing to explain.

gates.requirement: Research ethics board approval for interviews with patients, carers and staff

alternatives: Structured record review of readmissions only
Matched comparison of readmission rates with ward patients
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c2 to c5; the ethics application has not been submitted, so the gate is unknown and the action blocked.

summary: Qualitative interview study recommended; the ethics gate is unknown.
